ipq40xx/Gale: Return NULL for cbmem_top if DRAM is not initialized DRAM initialization on gale requires ipq blobs to be loaded from cbfs. vboot_locator first checks cbmem_find to see if cbmem is initialized and contains selected region info, else it falls back to vboot work buffer. Since cbmem_find calls into cbmem_top to identify the location of cbmem area, board/chipset is expected to return NULL until the backing store is ready, which in this case until DRAM is initialized in romstage, return NULL for cbmem_top. CHROMIUM: config: Renormalize the splitconfig Accepted defaults of chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig oldconfig I did a semi-thorough review of the differences in these configs from v3.18 -> v4.4 by running through chromeos/scripts/prepareconfig. Some notable diffs: These were dropped upstream: CONFIG_AVERAGE (a kernel library) CONFIG_X86_HT (subsumed into CONFIG_SMP for x86) CONFIG_BINFMT_ELF_RANDOMIZE_PIE + CONFIG_ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_RANDOMIZE_PIE (replaced by other features, which we have enabled) CONFIG_PM_RUNTIME (sucked into CONFIG_PM) CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL (it was beginning to be meaningless) CONFIG_KEYS_DEBUG_PROC_KEYS (tied to CONFIG_KEYS) New: CONFIG_BOUNCE There are quite a few other smaller changes, but nothing that really jumped out at me. A quick note on the overall diff: because there is only one 'flavour' for armel and arm64, all the chromiumos-{arm,arm64}.flavour.config entries are getting sucked into their respective common.config. This is expected at this stage, I suppose, and we'll probably get a different splitconfig once we start adding in new platforms (e.g., rk3399). BUG=none TEST=build/boot for samus; build other configs Change-Id: I94261e3311db832a6d2c108abcefd237f992e4c7 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/339650 Reviewed-by: Olof Johansson <olofj@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Avoid pointer arithmetic in calculating plane surface offset VMA offsets are 64 bits. Plane surface offsets are in ggtt and the hardware register to set this is thus 32 bits. Be explicit about these and convert carefully to from vma to final size. This will make sparse happy by not creating 32bit pointers out of 64bit vma offsets. Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mika Kuoppala <mika.kuoppala@intel.com> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1446204375-29831-1-git-send-email-mika.kuoppala@intel.com Reviewed-by: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 44eb0cb9620c6a53ec8e7073262e2af8079b727f) BUG=none TEST=build on x86 (32-bit) [Seeing errors like this: /mnt/host/source/src/third_party/kernel/v4.4/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c: In function 'intel_plane_obj_offset': /mnt/host/source/src/third_party/kernel/v4.4/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c:2969:11: error: cast to pointer from integer of different size [-Werror=int-to-pointer-cast] offset = (unsigned char *)vma->node.start; ^ ] Change-Id: Id8b96a0bf384e25c2250d4c391d49d8e7488095c Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/339654 Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>
